name: ANSI open-collector inverter
summary: Inverter triangle with output bubble and an open-circuit mark, needing an external pull-up to produce a high level.
description: This is an inverter whose output transistor can only pull low. On distinctive-shape schematics the triangle and bubble are retained and an open-collector or open-drain mark, often the underlined diamond, is placed inside or beside the outline. A pull-up resistor or load to a supply completes the circuit.

Open-drain inverters are used to drive indicator LEDs, relay inputs and shared interrupt or alarm lines, and to translate to a higher pull-up voltage within the device rating. The schematic should show the pull-up value and its supply rail next to the gate.
The output state with no pull-up is undefined when the transistor is off. A drawing that omits the pull-up is incomplete even though the gate symbol is correct.
readingNotes: Find the pull-up or load; without it the high level is undefined.
Check whether the output is shared with other open-collector outputs.
drawingChecklist: Mark the open-collector or open-drain output.
Show the pull-up and its supply.
Record the maximum output voltage and sink current from the datasheet.
distinction: The non-inverting open-collector buffer has no output bubble.
